_comment: Corpus for scripts/support_group_identity.py - the off-mode byte-identity gate of
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-02-support-sets-and-groups.md 3.7.
Everything here is generated by make_fixtures.py into ~1.2 KB plain 3MFs, so the corpus adds
no bulky binary data. The support configuration travels as CLI overrides rather than baked
into project files: the slicer's CLI accepts any print_config_def key as --key=value.
Two classes of input were tried and REJECTED by the plan's 5.1 experiment (same exe on both
sides of the comparison); see the Stage 2 status section:
- every .3mf under resources/handy_models/ segfaults the CLI on --slice, on an untouched
tree, with or without preset overrides. Pre-existing bug, unrelated to this work.
- resources/handy_models/OrcaToleranceTest.stl slices, but generates no support at all with
these presets AND is not self-reproducible (travel moves reorder between two runs).
- any plate holding more than one OBJECT is not self-reproducible: the print order of the
objects varies, moving whole blocks of G-code. Multi-PART objects (one object, several
MODEL_PART volumes) are reproducible, and they are what support groups are about.
common_args go on every case, and both are reproducibility requirements rather than taste -
the 5.1 experiment found each of them:
--disable-m73=1           M73 remaining-time comments are emitted when the estimate crosses
a minute boundary, and the estimate wobbles slightly between two
runs of ONE binary, shifting whole blocks of the file.
--slow-down-layer-time=0  the cooling slowdown scales feedrates by the estimated layer time,
which amplified that same wobble into differing G1 F values
(F9445 vs F9459) on small fast parts.
Neither touches geometry: every coordinate stays strictly compared.
Paths are relative to the repository root. 'args' are passed verbatim after the presets.
tree_classic was REMOVED. Classic tree support is not self-reproducible: baseline-against-
baseline on this very corpus gives 6.6% matching segments, 8 changed layers and 49 dirty
layers, run after run. Organic tree, normal supports and rafts are all stable through the
tolerance gate; only the classic tree path is not. 5.1 says to drop such a case and say so.
From Stage 3 on the corpus has TWO gates. Cases marked "groups": true carry support_group
data that the generator now acts on, so they are EXCLUDED from the default tolerance gate and
run under --gate groups instead, where they must DIFFER from the baseline (and only in
geometry: zero changed config rows). Every other case is off-mode and must stay within
tolerance. Stage 2's note below is kept for the record; the fixture it says did not exist now
does, and make_group_fixture.py builds both of its profiles.
There is deliberately NO case here carrying support_group data. Writing a loadable multi-part
fixture by hand did not work: a plain core-spec 3MF built from <component>s imports as one
ModelObject PER component, and per-part settings keyed on either the assembly object id or the
component object id were both ignored by the importer. Until a fixture is produced BY the
slicer itself, the group round trip is covered only by the unit tests, which build multi-volume
objects with add_volume. See the Stage 2 status section.

cases.name: group_parts
cases.comment: ON MODE from Stage 3 on. A project whose parts carry support_group and part-level support keys, produced by the SLICER ITSELF - see make_group_fixture.py. Through Stage 2 this was an OFF-mode case: the generator ignored those keys, so it had to come out exactly like a baseline that does not even know support_group and drops it on load. Stage 3 makes the tier A keys ACT, so the case moved to the groups gate: it must now DIFFER from the baseline, with zero changed config rows - the settings did not move, the geometry did - and the candidate must schedule a tool change to the group's own interface filament that the baseline never has. It deliberately carries no support_top_z_distance: that one acts through the soluble rule of 3.6 and would change far more than the interface.

cases.name: group_parts_matching
cases.comment: ON MODE, the regression case for the filament leak of 2c. Same fixture and same args as group_parts plus support filament matching (Chameleon) turned on, which is what the user's own project had. Chameleon and a support group write the same SupportLayer::interface_by_extruder map, so the group makes Chameleon stand down - but GCode.cpp's dominant-bucket pin still read that map as 'what Chameleon matched here' and pinned the layer's whole don't-care support to the group's filament. The result was the group's interface colour under BOTH parts and its filament in the support base as well, with the T1 tool change the plain expect_tool criterion asks for present the whole time. expect_tool_part is what sees it: T1 must draw the support interface on its own part and essentially none of the other part's.

cases.name: group_parts_geom
cases.comment: ON MODE, one filament. The same group as group_parts minus support_interface_filament, so the only thing that can move is the support INTERFACE geometry - no tool change, no second extruder, nothing that could be mistaken for a filament-ordering effect. The cleanest single statement of what Stage 3 does.

cases.name: group_single_part
cases.comment: ON MODE, one filament, ONE part. The object has a single MODEL_PART volume and that volume carries the group, so the default group owns no parts at all and there is no neighbour whose interface could make the result look wrong. It is the regression case for the claim-reach bug of 2c: a group whose claim does not cover the grid-stretched contacts silently hands them back to the default group, and on a single-part object nothing else in the G-code shows it. Same args as group_parts_geom so the two differ only in part count.

cases.name: over_support_off
cases.comment: OFF MODE for the over-support surfaces feature (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-over-support-surfaces.md). It sets exactly the inputs that feature reads - supports on, a NON-ZERO top Z distance, interface layers - so the object's underside is classified stBottomBridge and printed with the bridge settings, and it deliberately does NOT pass over_support_surfaces: the baseline build does not have that key, and the point of the case is that the default (off) leaves the output where it was. If the classifier ever fired without the switch, this is the case that would move.
